title: Text to Speech with ElevenLabs
summary: Send text to the provider and return binary audio without corrupting it.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Ultimate Guide to Using Eleven Labs API: Transform Text to Lifelike Speech in Minutes!

richText: Convert text into audio
Text to speech creates an audio recording from text.
ElevenLabs provides an HTTP API for this conversion.
POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id} accepts text in a JSON request body.
The voice ID selects the voice. model_id selects the model. output_format selects the audio format.
The response contains audio bytes. It is not a JSON object or a text string.
Use POST for an application endpoint that generates new audio. Generation performs an action and can consume paid quota.
Create the provider client
Keep the API key on the server. Send it in the provider’s xi-api-key header.
Allow only voice IDs that your application supports.
Set connection and read timeouts for the provider call.

example.title: Configure the ElevenLabs client
description: Use Spring Boot 3.2+, Spring Framework 6.1+, and Java 17.
Put this bean method in a @Configuration class.
Set elevenlabs.api-key from the ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable.
explanation: The client calls the fixed ElevenLabs API host.
The default xi-api-key header authenticates each request.
The connect timeout is three seconds. The read timeout is ten seconds.

richText: Return the audio response
Read audio into byte[] so the binary data remains intact.
Decoding audio bytes as a String can corrupt the recording.
Content-Type describes the returned audio format. Preserve it when your controller returns the bytes.

example.title: Request MP3 audio and return its bytes
description: This method body uses the configured speechClient and validated text and voiceId values.
It requests eleven_multilingual_v2 with mp3_44100_128 output. Verify that these choices are available to your account.
The containing controller method returns ResponseEntity<byte[]>.
explanation: The request sends the text and model ID as JSON.
toEntity(byte[].class) reads the response headers and binary body.
The checks reject an empty body or a non-audio Content-Type.
The controller returns the same bytes and audio media type. A browser can play or download them.

richText: Limit generation requests
Reject blank text and text longer than your application allows before calling the provider.
Require an explicit user action before sending private text to an external provider.
For long recordings, use streaming or a background job instead of holding the whole response in memory.
Treat authentication errors, rate limits, and timeouts as failures. Never return a JSON error body as audio.
A timeout can happen after generation starts. A retry may generate and charge twice.
Use provider-supported duplicate handling when available. Keep private text, audio, and API keys out of logs.
